# Issue review

## Scope

Independent relevance pass over the whole local backlog dump in `.github/issues/` — **122 files** — plus a completeness check of that dump against GitHub. Overlap with the earlier review from the same day is intentional: this pass re-derives every verdict from the current code instead of carrying forward the previous conclusions.

Reviewed revisions:

- `main`: `98ad5bf` (dependency bumps, `go-github/v91`, `go 1.26.0`) with the uncommitted rewrite of `.github/issues/` in the working tree — that working-tree content is what was reviewed.
- `fetcher`: `b0dd7d3` (`docs(status): explain push lock column and JSON filtering`). Note that the branch tip moved since the previous review recorded `1a7e92a` for the same commit subject.

Vocabulary. “Relevant” means work remains; priority is not assessed. “Relevant: bug confirmed” means the defect was reproduced against `main` during this pass. “Partial” means part of the expected behaviour exists. “Needs clarification” means there is not enough evidence either to close the issue or to start implementation. Closure as `not planned` is not evidence that the behaviour was fixed.

## Dump integrity

The dump is **incomplete**. GitHub holds 124 issues (46 open, 78 closed); the dump holds 122. Two open issues have no local file:

| Issue | Title | Created | Local file |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [#445](https://github.com/octomation/maintainer/issues/445) | fetch: prevent destructive clone reconciliation for occupied targets | 2026-08-13 | **missing** |
| [#446](https://github.com/octomation/maintainer/issues/446) | fetch: treat an empty upstream as a successful no-op | 2026-08-13 | **missing** |

Both are `type: bug` (severity `critical` and `major`), both describe the `fetch` stack, and both restate defects raised by the two code reviews of July 2026 — the recursive clone-failure cleanup and the fetch classification of a zero-ref upstream.

Everything else in the dump matches GitHub exactly. For all 122 shared issues, `status`, `title`, `labels`, and `updated_at` agree with the API with **zero** mismatches, and the dump contains no issue that GitHub does not have. So the dump is accurate but stale: it was taken before 2026-08-13 and not refreshed.

One classification nuance the dump's front matter cannot express: of the 78 closed issues, GitHub records 9 as `not planned` — [[issue-2|#2]], [[issue-9|#9]], [[issue-14|#14]], [[issue-15|#15]], [[issue-16|#16]], [[issue-32|#32]], [[issue-89|#89]], [[issue-99|#99]], [[issue-123|#123]] — and 69 as `completed`. The previous review grouped #14, #15, #16 and #32 with completed label work; they were in fact declined.

## Validation and sources

Everything below was executed during this pass, against `main` at `98ad5bf` unless stated otherwise.

- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` — all pass on `main` (Go 1.27.1, `GOFLAGS=-mod=readonly`). The previously recorded `TestTool_Load` failure no longer reproduces.
- A binary built from `main` was driven directly for the CLI checks. The live GitHub contribution calendar parsed successfully for 2022, 2024 and 2026, so the HTML scraper is currently working.
- `lookup` argument matrix: `lookup`, `lookup 2022`, `lookup 2022-02`, `lookup 2022-02-01` all panic; `lookup 2022/-1`, `lookup 2022/+10`, `lookup 2024-12-29/1`, `lookup now/3`, `lookup /3`, `lookup 2022-02-01/1` all render a table.
- `diff before.json after.json` over two hand-written snapshots reproduced the unsigned underflow.
- A temporary repository with a HEAD dated one day ahead reproduced the `suggest` panic, with the stack `assert.True ← NewRange ← Range.Since ← Suggest.func1`.
- A second temporary repository (HEAD `2024-03-05`) was used from its worktree and then from an unrelated directory with `GIT_DIR` set, to compare anchors.
- `makefile build` was run over a three-level include chain, and over a two-file include cycle.
- `snapshot 2021 2022`, `histogram 2022`, `diff --base=…`, and `lookup /2` were used to check argument arity, bar width, removed flags, and the table footer.
- On `fetcher`: `go build ./...` and `go test ./...` pass in full (20 packages). The regression tests named in the PoC sections of #445 and #446 exist and pass: `TestSync_CloneRefusesExistingTargetWithoutModification`, `TestSync_InspectAndUpdateRemotePreservePushURLs`, `TestSync_EmptyRemoteLifecycle`, `TestAdopter_ScanTreatsPushURLAsOrthogonalToIdentity`, `TestService_PlanReportsOccupiedCloneTargetAsConflict`, `TestService_PlanRecognisesCheckoutWithPushLock`, `TestService_ReconcilesEmptyRemoteAcrossApplyRuns`.
- Release state: the latest published release is `v0.1.0-rc11` (2024-03-30); no `v0.1.0` tag or release exists.
- The install URL in `README.md` points at the `master` ref; it still resolves (HTTP 200), so it is not a defect.

## Recommendations

Ordered by how much they change the state of the backlog.

1. **Re-pull the dump.** Add `issue-445.md` and `issue-446.md`, then note in both that the work is already implemented on `fetcher` and only needs to reach `main`. Until that happens the dump misrepresents the two highest-severity open bugs in the project.
2. **Do not close [[issue-81|#81]] as implemented.** Recursion works, but a cyclic include exhausts file descriptors and exits through `log.Fatal`. Either narrow the issue to the verified recursion and open a new one for cycle/repeat-include diagnostics, or keep it open with the cycle case as its acceptance criterion.
3. **Restate [[issue-155|#155]] as covering the default invocation.** The panic is not limited to a bare year: `maintainer github contribution lookup` with no argument at all — the form `docs/readme.md` advertises — panics too. This is the most visible defect on `main`.
4. **Merge the duplicates.** [[issue-148|#148]] into [[issue-133|#133]], preserving the reproduction; [[issue-69|#69]] into [[issue-175|#175]], preserving the link to [[issue-30|#30]]; consider folding [[issue-51|#51]] into [[issue-50|#50]].
5. **Treat the unsigned count type as one fix, not three.** [[issue-70|#70]], and the `%+d`-on-`uint` formatting behind it, sit under the same `HeatMap map[time.Time]uint` decision that also shapes [[issue-79|#79]] and [[issue-130|#130]] output. A signed diff type resolves [[issue-70|#70]] outright.
6. **Decide the supported Go version before touching anything else in CI.** [[issue-175|#175]] currently blocks any honest statement about compatibility, and both [[issue-30|#30]] and [[issue-69|#69]] depend on that answer.
7. **Close [[issue-40|#40]]'s remaining question explicitly.** It is the only closed issue whose gap (`.Range()`) is a deliberate open decision rather than historical residue; either add the method or record that the issue is finished without it.
